subject.title: feat: inspect background tasks across web and mobile

question: Should bounded task prompts remain readable through tasks.get with ordinary operator.read, or require a narrower or stronger authorization contract?
rationale: Task input can contain sensitive user text, and tests can prove truncation and internal-context stripping but cannot decide which operator scope should own this new disclosure.

options.title: Approve read-scoped prompts
options.body: Keep operator.read, explicitly document that task detail may expose bounded user input, and retain tests proving prompts never appear in lists or events and are stripped and capped on lookup.

options.title: Require stronger scope
options.body: Gate prompt-bearing task detail behind operator.admin or a dedicated sensitive-read scope while leaving ordinary task metadata on operator.read.

options.title: Omit prompts for now
options.body: Land cross-client status and output history without task input until a narrower authorization model is designed.

recommendation.title: Approve read-scoped prompts
recommendation.body: Keep operator.read, explicitly document that task detail may expose bounded user input, and retain tests proving prompts never appear in lists or events and are stripped and capped on lookup.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available history signal for the task-ledger RPC and Control UI contract affected by this choice.
